title: Chain Reaction Analysis and Stabilization Playbook - Kickoff
summary: Kickoff to walk through a recent chain-reaction outage where a combination of small KV-cache evictions and an aggressive autoscale policy produced long-tail token timeouts for inference. Agreed on immediate mitigations, instrumentation gaps, and a stabilization playbook with staged rollouts and an on-call drill.
action_items: Maya Patel - send mitigation checklist + initial trace bundle - due 2027-02-11
Jonah Reed - provide suggested runtime patch (small TTL bump + evict-by-size) and rollout notes - due 2027-02-12
Marcus Lee - run targeted soak test with cache-disabled and share metrics - due 2027-02-15
Lena Ortiz - update customer runbook draft with fallback triggers and paging rules - due 2027-02-14
Priya Nair - confirm business success criteria and acceptable latency SLOs for canary (percentiles + cost) - due 2027-02-10
Samir Das - collect kube-event history and autoscaler controller logs for 02/04 incident window and upload - due 2027-02-11
next_steps: Redwood to share raw inner-loop traces and KV eviction histograms
Schedule 90m stabilization workshop next week with oncall + infra + Redwood SE
Run a canary with TTL bump and modified autoscale window in staging then prod canary
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-09 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Platform: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Helios CTO), Marcus Lee (Helios SRE), Elena Varga (Platform PM), Samir Das (Infra), Olivia Chu (Security), Tomas Rivera (Oncall), Aaron B. (Dev)
Resources referenced: shared runbook draft (link), spike spreadsheet: https://redwood.internal/drive/helios-chain-reaction, traces: redwood-traces-20270204.tar.gz (shared)

00:00 Maya Patel: ok everyone thanks for carving out time, um, we're calling this a chain reaction kickoff to avoid the long ramble, we've got 58 minutes on the calendar, uh quick round robin intro?
00:22 Priya Nair: Priya here, CTO, i'll be listening for business impact and what we need for a clean SLA story, we had two customer-facing degradation windows on friday so wanted to move quick here
00:34 Marcus Lee: Marcus — SRE — i'll own root cause artifacts and run the soak tests we talked about, thanks
00:40 Jonah Reed: Jonah from Redwood SE, i'll go through the traces we pulled and the hypothesis around eviction-aligned spikes
00:48 Lena Ortiz: Lena, CSM, i'll coordinate follow ups and timeline for the stabilization playbook
00:56 Elena Varga: Elena, platform PM. i'm most interested in trigger thresholds and rollback criteria
01:05 Maya Patel: cool, agenda: quick timeline, hypothesis for what propagated faults, immediate mitigations, instrumentation gaps, and then playbook + action items. Jonah, do you want to start on timeline?
01:18 Jonah Reed: yeah, sure. so we reconstructed the window starting at 02/04 03:12 UTC, small uptick in short-lived requests, nothing huge by qps but we see a correlated spike of KV cache evictions at the same time. the eviction bursts seem to coincide with autoscaler resizing events that trimmed pooled GPU workers. when the workers were reaped the KV cache drops and subsequent requests hit cold-kv plus a cascade of longer KV fetch latency which elongated token emission and pushed requests past our 2s token window, triggering client-side retries. so retries amplified the load and we had a classic feedback loop.
03:05 Priya Nair: when you say "cold-kv" are you meaning the local KV cache on the serving nodes or the centralized cache?
03:12 Jonah Reed: local per-worker KV cache. it's an LRU with size limits per process, so it's sensitive to worker churn. we also noticed that the autoscale policy had a very short stabilization window, like 30s, and was trimming pods aggressively during small qps drops.
03:40 Marcus Lee: just to add, our metrics show a CPU spike on the autoscaler leader around the same time — possibly controller throttling. also kube events show OOMKilled for one adapter pod a minute before the eviction storm. so the chain starts a bit earlier than client retries.
04:10 Maya Patel: interesting, so there were two immediate levers: reduce worker churn (autoscale config) and make KV cache less fragile (TTL bump, size heuristic). any concerns about cost if we increase cache size or reduce scale aggressiveness?
04:30 Priya Nair: cost is a concern but uptime is first priority for the next 72 hours. we can accept a small lift, we just need the rollback plan if cost goes crazy.
04:45 Elena Varga: and we need precise metrics to know when to revert, so suggested canary thresholds and telemetry we'll need.
04:55 Jonah Reed: agreed. practical mitigation options we suggested in the shared doc: 1) short-term: bump per-worker KV size + increase TTL from 60s -> 300s, 2) adjust autoscale stabilization from 30s to 180s and add a min-replicas floor during business hours, 3) tune retry logic client-side (linear backoff and max 2 retries), 4) add a temporary admission reject for super-long tail requests to avoid amplification.
06:05 Samir Das: quick Q — changing TTL seems straightforward, but per-worker size changes require a restart for the worker process, correct? that means a rolling restart which could itself cause churn if done badly.
06:22 Jonah Reed: yeah, it will trigger rolling restarts if you change the env var or container config; we provided rollout guidance: do a small staging canary of 10% traffic, validate eviction histograms and 99th percentile token time, then proceed to 30% then full. keep on-call engaged.
06:46 Tomas Rivera: also remember our last restart window is during business hours so we should avoid making big changes during our peak if possible.
06:55 Maya Patel: good call. Marcus, can you share the event logs and OOM traces?
07:02 Marcus Lee: i'll upload the kube events + kubelet logs to the shared folder by EOD, i've already pulled the autoscaler controller logs and will include them.
07:10 Olivia Chu: from security side — any config changes that touch KMS or telemetry need approval; are we touching encryption keys or logs?
07:20 Jonah Reed: no keys. this is all eviction/TTL and autoscale tuning. we'll only read existing traces. nothing touches KMS or secret rotation.
07:28 Olivia Chu: ok, noted — i'll still need to sign off on the rollout plan.
07:35 Maya Patel: instrumentation gaps — we found limited distributed trace sampling, no flamegraphs for the 02/04 window, and token-level timing across the chain wasn't captured. that's on us and we will produce higher fidelity traces for the next meeting.
08:00 Elena Varga: can you also include the request id mapping so we can correlate customer sessions? some of our customers reported retries but we couldn't map them to infra ids.
08:12 Jonah Reed: yes, we'll add the correlation id mapping in next upload. current traces have partial mapping which may be why some spans are missing.
08:20 Priya Nair: on the stabilization playbook, i want explicit criteria: what percentile improvements we need to see in staging before moving to prod canary, and what cost delta is acceptable.
08:35 Maya Patel: suggested canary success criteria: 95th token latency reduced to under 600ms (from 980ms in incident), error rate < 0.1% for canonical workloads, and cost increase < 15% for the canary window. does that sound reasonable?
09:00 Priya Nair: yes those seem sane, maybe 99th under 1.2s as a secondary check.
09:10 Aaron B.: tiny thing from devs — some clients have aggressive retry loops that do immediate retries; we should push small client-side change for exponential backoff in parallel with server-side mitigations.
09:23 Maya Patel: agreed, this reduces amplification risk. action: Aaron will push a client patch with backoff set to initial 300ms, multiplier 2, max retries 2, and we will evaluate.
09:34 Aaron B.: yep, i'll queue that and schedule a quick deploy Tuesday.
09:40 Jonah Reed: one further note — we saw a secondary path where long KV fetchs map to cold storage reads in a different layer; we need to check how often the cold-read path is invoked during eviction storms. if cold-read percentage spikes, we may need a separate mitigation (prefetch or warm-up).
10:00 Marcus Lee: i'll add cold-read counters to the telemetry and run a scoped replay test.
10:08 Maya Patel: ok, let's talk about the stabilization playbook timeline: immediate mitigations (TTL bump + autoscale stabilization) to be tested in staging in 48 hours, then a 4-hour prod canary, then a 24-72 hour observation window.
10:22 Priya Nair: that's fine. we want the canary to happen in off-peak and with an automatic rollback if 95th > 900ms or error rate doubles.
10:35 Maya Patel: noted. Jonah, can you summarize the rollout steps you'll provide?
10:42 Jonah Reed: yes: 1) staging patch: TTL 300s + per-worker size + autoscale stabilizer increased to 180s, 2) run 1h soak with synthetic load + real shadowed traffic, check eviction histograms and token p50/p95/p99, 3) 10% prod canary for 4 hours, check criteria, 4) 30% prod for 6 hours, 5) full. rollback triggers: 95th > 900ms or error rate > 0.2%. we will include exact kubectl rollout commands and healthchecks in the doc.
12:05 Lena Ortiz: i'll version the runbook and store it in Helios/Runbooks/stabilization-v1. Lena will also add who to page at each threshold.
12:15 Priya Nair: on paging, remember to include SRE on-call escalation matrix and an exec alert path for customer-impacting incidents.
12:25 Tomas Rivera: can we get an automated runbook button that triggers the rollback playbook? right now it's manual.
12:35 Jonah Reed: Redwood has an API endpoint to trigger automated rollback via the control plane, but we need your ACLs enabled; we'll send the minimal perms required.
12:42 Olivia Chu: send me the ACL spec and i'll review.
12:48 Maya Patel: instrumentation to produce: token-level timings, eviction histograms, per-worker cache sizes over time, autoscaler event history, kubelet OOM snapshots, and client retry traces. Jonah will put it together.
13:05 Marcus Lee: i'll run the replay and soak tests and upload metrics; Tomas will monitor the canary.
13:12 Elena Varga: timeline recap?
13:15 Maya Patel: sure — by EOD 02/11 Redwood will upload the full trace bundle and mitigation checklist; Helios will upload kube events and confirm business SLOs by 02/10; small client retry change to be queued by Aaron for 02/11; staging canary by 02/13; prod canary earliest 02/15 in off-peak.
13:45 Priya Nair: okay, good. final question: do we anticipate the need for a code change in the runtime to handle warm-starting KV caches?
13:55 Jonah Reed: we may need a minor runtime change to support on-demand prefetch; that's a medium-term item, not for the emergency canary. we'll open a ticket and include a patch plan.
14:10 Maya Patel: perfect. any other blockers from security or compliance?
14:17 Olivia Chu: just the ACL spec and final rollout doc. otherwise clear.
14:23 Maya Patel: great — i'll send notes, action items, and the shared artifact links. we will schedule the 90m stabilization workshop for next Tuesday 16:00 UTC. thanks everyone.
14:35 Priya Nair: thanks all.
14:40 Meeting ends
